Returns authenticated user's carts or guest carts by session_id.
Only one cart per user is typical, but multiple may exist with different currencies.

For guest checkout, use session_id.

If the product already exists in cart, quantity is updated and item is merged.
Cart totals are automatically recalculated.

Cart totals are automatically recalculated.

delete.description:

Cart totals are automatically recalculated.

post.description:
Converts the cart into an order. Validates cart contents, applies shipping,
deducts inventory, and marks cart as converted.
Returns the created order with all details.

status_counts.description:
Counts ignore the status filter so each status tab can show its
own total; they still honour the date range and search.

months.description:
Months that have orders at all, so the month filter can list
real options instead of guessing from the current page.

post.summary:
Approving moves an order into the working state. It used to write
'approved', which is outside the canonical set in
UpdateOrderRequest::STATUSES and would leave the row with no matching
filter tab in the admin UI
Rejecting cancels the order. Previously wrote 'rejected' — see approve()

discount_total.description:
Order-level amounts. Line items drive the subtotal; these adjust
it into the grand total.

unit_price.description:
Cast before formatting: Postgres returns decimal columns as
strings, which number_format() rejects under strict_types.

id.description: `id` stays the uuid — routes bind on it (Order::getRouteKeyName).

order_number.description: The human-facing reference staff and customers actually quote.

total.description:
Cast before formatting: Postgres returns decimal columns as
strings, which number_format() rejects under strict_types.

subtotal.description: Breakdown behind the total, for the order detail summary panel.

shipping_address.description:
Snapshot taken at checkout; there is no addresses data yet, so
this is usually null and the UI falls back to a placeholder.

images.description:
Omitted rather than sent as [] when not loaded, so a client can
tell "this product has no gallery" from "the list endpoint didn't
 ship one" — index() stays light and only sends `thumbnail`.

promotion_ids.description:
Ids drive the product form's promotion checkboxes; the nested
objects save it a second request for the labels. Both omitted
when the relation is not loaded, so the light index() payload
does not imply "this product has no promotions".

orders_count.description:
withCount/withSum leave these null when the row has no orders, so
both coalesce to zero.

usage_remaining.description:
Aggregate capacity, useful for "only 5 left" storefront urgency.
The exact redemption ledger stays admin-only.

email.description: At least one of email/phone is required.

first_name.description: Naming: 'name' is a convenience that the User mutator splits into first/last.

phone.description:
`users.phone` is uniquely indexed, so a blank one has to arrive as
null rather than '' — two empty strings would collide.

password.description:
The admin form has no password field: when it is omitted the
controller generates one, and the customer resets it themselves.

promotion_ids.description:
Promotions applied to this product. Validated against `coupons`:
the admin promotions API is coupon-backed (PromotionController).

image.description:
Capped at 255 to match the varchar column — a longer URL would
pass validation and then fail at the driver.

variants.description: Nested variants (replaces the existing pattern of separate endpoints).

payment_status.description:
Payment state is recorded here rather than at creation — a new
order cannot already be paid, failed or refunded.

replace_variants.description:
Variant array. When `replace_variants` is omitted or true, the
submitted set replaces the existing set. When false, the
controller treats the array as additive.

Promotions applied to this product. Validated against `coupons`:
the admin promotions API is coupon-backed (PromotionController).
